passages.provision_quote: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase
passages.note: Bill text page of the vote; prints the operative rent-cap clause but names no voter.
Assembly Floor concurrence vote lists Robert Rivas among the Ayes; names no provision text.
passages.tally_quote: Ayes Count 48 Noes Count 26 NVR Count 5

rows.reasoning: Rivas voted Aye in the Assembly (Appropriations 05/08/19, Third Reading 05/29/19, and Concurrence in Senate Amendments 09/11/19) on AB 1482 (2019-2020), which caps rent increases and adds just-cause eviction protections statewide while its own findings clause states the act 'is not intended to expand or limit the authority of local governments to establish local policies regulating rents' and lets more-protective local just-cause ordinances continue to apply, extending baseline coverage to units with no prior rent regulation. This matches 'Strengthen existing rent stabilization and extend coverage to more units,' not rung 1 (the bill exempts new construction, single-family homes, dorms, and deed-restricted affordable units, so it does not cover 'all rental units communitywide') and not rung 3 (the act is a new statewide expansion of protections, not a maintenance of the status quo).
